analysis.title: Global Economics & Markets Outlook 2027-2028
key_insights: UBS calls the global economy 'solid but unusually narrow'. The AI infrastructure build-out has offset the 2025 tariff and 2026 energy headwinds, and drives over half of global trade growth and nearly half of YTD global equity gains (MSCI ACWI).

Global growth is forecast to pick up from 3.2% to 3.5% in 2027 (Q4/Q4). The 'rest of the world' adds 38bp, of which 29bp comes from Saudi Arabia and the UAE on an assumed recovery in oil and gas volumes. Saudi growth swings from -4.6% to 10.4%.

Bottom-up aggregation of UBS equity analysts' forecasts gives about $1.75-1.8 trillion of hyperscaler capex in 2027, versus about $1 trillion in 2026. That is over 5% of US GDP, and five companies account for 85% of it. Surging memory prices add $463bn to 2026-27E capex, so part of the increase is price rather than extra compute.

The two biggest risks to the UBS forecast are a delay or reprofiling of data-centre spending (public opposition, 415 active local moratoriums, a power gap of about 100GW by 2030) and an unresolved Middle East conflict. The report also models a bond market stress scenario.

AI adoption is described as 'a mile wide but an inch deep'. 80% of executives use AI but for only 2.1 hours a week, 2% of firms account for half of AI spending, and enterprise adoption is about 20%. US productivity has grown 1.3% annualised over the last three quarters and 2.1% over four quarters, with TFP stalling.

US corporate profits are at 14.5% of GDP, the highest since 1947. The last three years of profit growth fall outside the macro models, and about 90% of the recent increase comes from tech and financials (the rest mostly oil and mining). S&P 500 net income has risen to about 90% of economy-wide after-tax profits, from roughly half.

Policy: UBS expects monetary policy to stay restrictive through end-2027 with hikes reversed in 2028. It expects the Fed to hike 25bp in December and January, to 4.25-4.50%, then pause. Fed Chair Warsh favours no forward guidance. Core PCE is projected at 2.5% by YE27 and headline PCE at 2.1%.

Equities: UBS expects about 12% S&P 500 returns in 2027E and favours Nasdaq over Russell 2000, Industrials over Consumer Discretionary, and Growth and Quality over Value. It expects broadening into AI-adjacent sectors (Industrials, Financials, Health Care) rather than a rotation away from AI. The base case assumes no valuation support.

Earnings are the key question. 2026 MSCI ACWI earnings growth ran at the 91st percentile of history against GDP growth at the 29th percentile. 12m forward US earnings growth expectations are 17.8% for 2027 and 16.9% for 2028. Falling earnings revisions have historically hurt markets when starting expectations are high.

EM: MSCI EM return forecast of about 20% in 2027, with EPS growth of 38% in 2027E and 22% in 2028E. About three-quarters comes from Korea and Taiwan. Korea is preferred over India. MSCI China trades at 9.5x 12m forward P/E, 1.2 standard deviations below its average, after a tech-led sell-off.

Chips and memory: UBS sees memory undersupplied until 2Q28, with prices peaking around mid-2028 and rising more than 600% through the cycle. Five-year cumulative FCF is forecast at 100-180% of market cap for the three large memory makers, which trade at about 4x NTM P/E. SK Hynix plans to return at least 50% of cumulative FCF in 2025-27 and Samsung 50% in 2026. Semis and the Momentum factor were 'the same trade' this year, and UBS says the liquidity shock that hurt Momentum is nearly past.

Cloud revenue growth accelerated to about 100% q/q annualised in Q3 (+$86bn on a roughly $540bn run rate, nearly triple Q1). UBS says AI monetisation needs $2-4tr of annual revenue to justify $6-8tr of 2025-30 capex, and estimates about $2.4-2.5tr at the midpoint. UBS cloud revenue estimates are about 15% above consensus for the next four quarters.

Fixed income: UBS says terminal rates are priced too high and expects front-end and belly yields to fall. It expects a bull-steepening US curve as term premium rises. 10y yield forecasts for YE2027 are 4.80% (UST), 3.25% (Bund) and 5.00% (gilt). Europe favours flatteners (2s10s ESTR). Bond returns should reach mid-single digits in 2027 and bond-equity correlation should turn negative.

Portfolio allocation: bonds returned -2.6% annualised over 5 years against 12% for MSCI ACWI. AAII equity allocations are above 70% against 16% for government bonds. Risk parity and mean-variance approaches suggest cutting equity exposure from just over 85% in 2026 to 70% in 2027 and just under 50% in 2028.

Energy: the base case is Brent averaging $80/bbl in 2027 and TTF gas at EUR45/MWh. More than 70% of the over 20 Mb/d of oil flowing through Hormuz pre-conflict is reaching markets, LNG flows are at about 20% of pre-conflict levels, global oil inventories are down about 8% and below the five-year range, and refining outages are about 11 Mb/d. Risks are skewed to higher prices, but a sharp fall in oil is flagged as a larger risk to UBS's recommendations than higher energy prices.

FX and gold: UBS sees no clear evidence of de-dollarisation. Gold is not behaving as a diversifier, with positive beta to the S&P 500. UBS targets XAUUSD at $5,000 by end-2027, EURUSD at 1.10, and USDJPY at 160 by year-end 2027. It expects the BoJ to hike to 2% by 3Q27 and the 10y JGB to reach 3.2%.

Volatility: low index volatility is described as structural, driven by tech concentration, low correlation and high dispersion. Leveraged ETFs, short-dated option-writing and defined-outcome ETFs amplify it, and markets are 'persistently more fragile'. Rates volatility is repricing higher under the Warsh Fed, and UBS favours long V2X over VIX into the French election.

Politics: Democrats gained control of Congress in the US midterms. US federal funding expires December 11 and the debt ceiling is expected to bind in Q1 2027. France's presidential election is on 18 April and 2 May 2027, with Marine Le Pen leading polls. French debt is 115.7% of GDP, the 2025 deficit was 5.4% of GDP, and UBS sees OAT spreads around 150bp at best.

Credit: UBS expects US private credit default rates to rise 300bp to 7-8% by end-2027, with about 21% of debt maturing in two years and layered financing of roughly $1.5tn. Base case is dispersion rather than contagion. It prefers European IG over US IG and closed its long CDX HY protection recommendation.

Scenarios: oil at $150 cuts 2027 global growth by 40bp. Oil at $60 adds only about 10bp. US 10y at 6.5% cuts 2028 growth by 120bp. An AI disappointment with a 25% S&P correction is the most damaging, cutting 2027-28 global growth by about 2.1pp, putting 12 economies into recession and taking HY spreads near 700bp, EURUSD towards 1.20 and gold towards $7,000.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscalers and chips are the nucleus of the AI trade. The 2026 derating despite strong earnings gives some comfort. Memory and leading-edge foundry are favoured.
Data-centre suppliers are expanding their own capacity, and Industrials earnings revisions are positive (about 1%) while Consumer Discretionary revisions are negative.
Energy bills, interest costs and weak real wages squeeze households. Revisions are below zero and positioning is increasingly crowded.
AI-adjacent broadening, strong profit contribution and European bank upgrades. Financials would benefit most from an oil price reversal.
Listed as an AI-adjacent sector UBS favours.
More unprofitable companies, higher median net debt/EBITDA, and greater sensitivity to financing costs than the Nasdaq 100.
Model and software companies face greater disruption risk. Leveraged software borrowers face disproportionate EBITDA declines from modest revenue pressure.

earnings_insights: UBS: 2026 MSCI ACWI earnings growth is tracking about 15-20% (estimate), with the year starting at 12m forward growth expectations of 15.1% for the US versus likely realised growth of 34.7%.
UBS (consensus/forecast): 12m forward US earnings growth expectations are 17.8% for 2027 and 16.9% for 2028.
UBS: MSCI EM EPS growth forecast of 38% in 2027E and 22% in 2028E, with about three-quarters from Korea and Taiwan.
Consensus (cited by UBS): Stoxx 600 EPS growth of nearly 20% in 2026 and 10% in 2027.
UBS: Nasdaq 100 12m forward EPS has risen about 2x more than Russell 2000 EPS over the past 12 months or more. NDX has a HOLT NTM cash flow ROI of about 30% against about 10% for RTY.
UBS: Tech LTM operating cash flow is up nearly 40% y/y. Buybacks tend to follow OCF with a 2-4 quarter lag, and Nvidia and Micron alone could be over 25% of total LTM US buybacks (UBS estimate).
UBS: for the three large memory producers, five-year cumulative FCF is forecast at 100-180% of current market cap (the essay summary says 80-160%) while trading at about 4x NTM P/E.
UBS: AI hardware earnings in China have 12-15% upgrades over the past three months. STAR50 is down YTD despite over 200% y/y earnings growth.
UBS: 44% of S&P 500 companies expect capex growth above 10% in bottom-up data.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 3.2%, with most of the acceleration from the Middle East volume recovery, so it is a narrow base.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.7% QoQ annualised through September (hard data about 2.3%, soft data 3.1% in September and 2.6% in October)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Close to trend, with momentum fading in both hard and soft data.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.5% in 2026 (UBS estimate), 2.1% over the four quarters to Q3
macro_indicators.interpretation: Resilient, underpinned by AI capex.
Energy-driven overshoot. Relief is expected from spring 2027 as the gasoline base effects are lapped.
Down 0.4pp since September 2025.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.1% current; 2.5% by end-2027 (forecast); headline PCE 2.1% by end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Core PCE is up 0.3pp since September 2025. UBS expects inflation to approach the Fed's target range by H2 2027.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.25-4.50% after hikes in December and January
macro_indicators.interpretation: A three-hike recalibration including the September hike, then a pause into 2028.
Falling policy expectations offset by higher term premium.
Bund curve flattening.
Inflation-driven yields.
BoJ hiking to 2% by 3Q27 is mostly priced in the forwards.
Japan has exited deflation.
Fiscal impulse adds 30bp. Downside risk from energy prices.
Down 12.6% from 2026. Upside scenario $120+ or $150, downside scenario $60.
Upside EUR55, downside EUR35.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Over 5% of US GDP, with five companies at 85% of the total.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since 1947, about double the mid-1980s share.
Driven by debt service costs.

macro_indicators.reading: two more 25bp hikes in December and March
macro_indicators.interpretation: The ECB's headline inflation focus requires high front-end rates.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.75% in December, 3.0% in January, 3.0% at end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Follows the 25bp October hike to 2.5%.
Refinancing needs for 2020-21 vintages and software borrowers.

crypto_views: Stablecoin issuance doubled since 2024 to about $300bn by Sep 2025 (IMF), and the BIS puts capitalisation at $320bn by end-May 2026 against about $19tn of US bank deposits.

UBS estimates economic payments at about 4% of raw stablecoin transaction volume in 2026 YTD, flat versus 2025, below about 5% in 2024 and about 10% in 2023. Crypto trading remains the dominant use case.
99.5% of stablecoins are dollar-pegged (UBS research), so wider adoption could reinforce rather than threaten dollar dominance.
Payment adoption by AI agents could change stablecoin usage and is flagged as a development to monitor.

trade_ideas.rationale: NDX has underperformed RTY since early October despite about 2x the EPS revision strength, and NDX P/E has fallen toward 2022 levels.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharply lower rates for good reasons, or a growth/AI disappointment.

trade_ideas.description: Long MSCI World Industrials vs MSCI World Consumer Discretionary
trade_ideas.rationale: Data-centre suppliers are expanding their capacity, reshoring is supportive, and consumer revisions and positioning are weak.

trade_ideas.description: Long MSCI Korea vs MSCI India
trade_ideas.rationale: Korea's memory and semiconductor stocks (66% of index) sit at an AI bottleneck, and the market expects only 40% of UBS's 3-year EBITDA forecasts.
trade_ideas.risk: Concerns about datacentre rollout pace after the US midterms.

trade_ideas.description: Long V2X vs VIX via April expiry ATMF straddle swaps (spot V2X 21.3, VIX 25.6)
trade_ideas.rationale: French election risk, the 2017 record volatility risk premium, clear voting dates and no immediate ECB backstop.
trade_ideas.risk: US volatility rising more than European volatility.

trade_ideas.description: Long US Growth & Quality vs US Value, favoured via UBS Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) vs Expensive Fundamentals (UBEQEXFN)
trade_ideas.rationale: The basket trades at 16x P/E vs 21x with 14% forward sales CAGR vs 5%, 33% CFROI vs 6%, and 6% FCF yield vs -2%.

trade_ideas.description: Long earnings momentum factor in Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings momentum is Europe's best-performing factor since at least 2010, and revisions mattered more than yields across 15 of 17 sectors.

trade_ideas.description: US rates: 1y forward 5s30s SOFR curve steepener
trade_ideas.rationale: Long-end steepeners offer better risk-reward ahead of the last Fed hike, and duration supply adds steepening pressure.

trade_ideas.description: European rates: pay-side flattener, enter EUR STR 2s10s at 17bp, target -20bp, stop 35bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Euro area inflation peak is still ahead, German fiscal stimulus adds duration supply, and a hawkish ECB should pin down the long end.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy shock and flight to quality pushing 10y rates down.

trade_ideas.description: Receive MXN 2y2y rates, targeting a 75-100bp decline from 8.4%
trade_ideas.rationale: Markets price 120bp of Banxico hikes over two years, which looks too aggressive given benign core inflation.

trade_ideas.description: Receive AUD 3y2y vs pay NZD 3y2y (entry +67bp, target +30bp, stop +75bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: The spread is wide of the +36bp fair value estimate, which UBS expects to tighten toward +7bp by end-27.
trade_ideas.risk: Expansionary AUD fiscal policy, or RBNZ staying dovish.

trade_ideas.description: Long EU IG vs US IG (1.8 x 1, duration and FX hedged), with an Q2'27 spread target of 95bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads reached about 110bp at the wides, and Europe has priced more of the rates shock than the US.

trade_ideas.description: Long SOAF 49s vs BRAZIL 47s, targeting a z-spread gap of -45bp (from -4bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: Diverging debt trajectories and Brazil bond supply risk.
trade_ideas.risk: South Africa ANC elective conference in December 2027 and political uncertainty.

trade_ideas.description: Long XAUEUR 4055 digital call, 30 June 2027, for 19.9% of payout (spot ref 3585.95)
trade_ideas.rationale: Gold's October break in correlation looks temporary, and French uncertainty should weigh on EUR (UBS EURUSD target 1.10).
trade_ideas.risk: Maximum loss is the option premium.

trade_ideas.description: Long CHFJPY 187.55 digital put, 30 June 2027, for 19.40% of payout (spot ref 193.89)
trade_ideas.rationale: BoJ/MoF and SNB intervention should cap upside in the pair and allow a move lower in a euro area stress scenario.
trade_ideas.risk: Maximum loss is the upfront premium.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBPSEK 13.40 call with European knockout barrier at 14.10, 30 June expiry, offered at 0.35% of notional (spot ref 13.1193)
trade_ideas.rationale: GBP is supported by a higher policy rate and better capital flows than SEK.
trade_ideas.risk: Central bank divergence, and the knockout barrier at the 20-year range high.

risk_factors: AI capex delay or reprofiling from public opposition to data centres, local moratoriums and power shortages (about 100GW gap by 2030).
An AI disappointment triggering a 25% S&P correction. This is the most damaging scenario, with household equity wealth around 230% of GDP.
The Middle East conflict not resolving, with oil to $120-150 and inventories below the five-year range.
A bond market shock with US 10y at 6.5% from fiscal concerns, heavy hyperscaler issuance, and a rising r*.
A falling earnings revision cycle when expectations are already high (above 15%).
Rising public debt, with DM debt growing 2pp of GDP a year and US interest spending at a 26-year high.
French fiscal and political risk ahead of the April/May 2027 election, with OAT spreads at risk of widening.
Momentum and semis crowding, and sensitivity to liquidity shocks.
Private credit refinancing and liquidity stress, and BDC redemptions.
Super El Niño pushing up food prices, affecting Colombia, Peru and Europe.
A sharp fall in oil would revive consumption and broaden investment beyond Tech, which UBS flags as a larger risk to its recommendations than higher energy prices.
vol_and_positioning: Spot reference for the V2X vs VIX trade: V2X at 21.3, VIX at 25.6. Suggested implementation through V2X vs VIX ATMF straddle swaps on an April expiry, which captures the 2 May second round. March expiry would not capture the first round in its 30-day forward window.
The volatility risk premium during the 2017 French election was the highest on record for a sovereign election.
Index volatility was unusually subdued until last week, with low correlations offsetting high single-stock volatility. Both were reported to have changed last week.
UBS sees 12m realised USDCNH volatility at 2.4%, the lowest since the August 2015 devaluation.
Japanese FX intervention is lowering USDJPY volatility. UBS favours a selective approach to FX volatility trades.
Gold XAU risk reversal skews are now bid for puts over calls.
Equity allocations above 70% against 16% for government bonds is the widest gap in 25 years. EM active funds are overweight India and sharply underweight Korea.
China AI hardware fast-money positioning is back to beginning-of-year levels and HK short interest is the highest on record.
Consumer discretionary crowding is elevated, with a wide gap to industrials.

UBS sees selling technology equity volatility as potentially attractive (semiconductor stocks and indices have high volatility and prospects for capital returns), while selling broad equity volatility is unattractive.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict: Strait of Hormuz disruption, with more than 70% of pre-conflict flows reaching markets, LNG at about 20% of normal, and a June MoU referenced as a template for normalisation.
US-Iran: the oil $60 scenario assumes a US/Iran deal regulating Hormuz traffic and no further attacks on infrastructure after the US midterms.
US midterms: Democrats gained control of Congress, raising shutdown, debt ceiling and AI/data-centre oversight risks.
France: presidential election on 18 April and 2 May 2027 with Marine Le Pen leading polls, plus legislative elections in June or July 2027.
US-China trade truce set to expire on 10 January 2027, with a possible quadrupling of tariff rates if it lapses.
USMCA: the US decided not to renew in July, the agreement stays in force, and annual reviews and bilateral tariff negotiations continue.
Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods were modified on 23 October 2026, with the weighted average rate staying at 11.7%.
US data-centre moratoriums: 406-415 active local moratoriums and a quarter of state governors have issued executive orders limiting construction.
Argentina presidential election in October 2027 and Mexico midterms in June 2027.
Brazil: Lula won the runoff with 51.8% of valid votes, and a finance minister appointment is expected possibly in early December.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue growth near 100% annualised in Q3, UBS cloud estimates about 15% above consensus, and 2027 capex near $1.75-1.8tn with AI compute revenue potentially clearing the $2-4tr hurdle.
tension_points.bear_case: Public opposition and moratoriums, a power gap of about 100GW, concentrated spending (5 firms at 85%), and expectations already at 17.8% for 2027 earnings growth. AI disappointment is the most damaging scenario.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Genuine data-centre capex cuts and weaker 3-year growth, or downward 12m and 24m forward earnings revisions that persist.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects terminal rates to be repriced lower, with front-end and belly yields falling and the curve bull-steepening as inflation falls toward 2.5% core PCE by H2 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Term premium may rise on heavier Treasury and IG duration supply and weaker foreign official demand, and the market assumes a higher r* from capex and productivity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation stuck near 3.0% after six months of waiting could prompt another sequence of Fed hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: NDX has stronger EPS growth, quality and AI exposure, with net cash and buyback growth.
tension_points.bear_case: The oil price falling sharply could revive consumption and benefit small caps and global equities over US large caps and tech.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp decline in oil, sharply lower rates for good reasons, or growth/AI disappointment.
